terms.comment: Any contest, friendly or hostile, of strength or of wits (Lewis & Short); an athletic competition is āthlētārum certāmen (Traupman 62).
A contest for first place; plain certāmen serves where the context is clear.

phrases.latin: quanta studia dēcertantium sunt! quanta ipsa certāmina! ut illī efferuntur laetitiā, cum vīcērunt! ut pudet victōs!
phrases.english: how keen they are to compete! what contests! how they exult when they win! how ashamed the losers are!

phrases.latin: hōc certāmine puer quīdam audentior cēterīs in ulteriōra tendēbat
phrases.english: in this competition one boy, bolder than the rest, swam further out

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 44, 62, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).: p. 296.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-plinius), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
